question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

This is the boy **who he stole** the purse.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains a redundancy issue with the phrase "**who he stole**."
 
• The pronoun "**he**" is unnecessary because "**who**" already serves as the subject of the relative clause.
 
• The correct construction is "**who stole**," which eliminates the redundancy and maintains grammatical accuracy.
 
• Thus, **Option 4** is the best choice to improve the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"This is the boy who stole the purse."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "who had stole"** – This option is incorrect because "had stole" is grammatically incorrect. The correct past perfect form would be "had stolen."
 
• **Option 2: "which stole"** – This option is incorrect because "which" is used for things, not people. The correct pronoun for a person is "who."
 
• **Option 3: "whom stole"** – This option is incorrect because "whom" is used as an object, not as the subject of a clause. The correct choice here is "who."
